page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Running head centred at the top: "AD LECTOREM." Two marginal notes in the right margin: "Postellus." beside the first line, and "Michaelis Servetus." beside the third and fourth lines. Catchword "tim" at the lower right. Gathering signature ")( 3" at the foot.

l.i: Postellus vero, homo ex omnibus quantumvis monstrosis hæresibus veluti conflatus, ausus est publice profiteri, Iohannam, nescio quam, Venetam, venisse servandis mulieribus, sicut Christus vivos redemisset.

Sed vel inprimis Michaël[?] ille Servetus, Hispanus, hæresiarcha, et sacra Triadis, h. e. omnis vera deitatis hostis, adeoq; teterrimum illud monstrum ex omnibus omnium temporum hæresibus conflatū, postquam aliquot annis hinc inde medicinam faciens oberrasset, tectus Michaelis Villanovani nomine, horrendas multas blasphemias sparsit. Cum Sabellio personas & essentiam confundebat: Cum Samosateno docebat, Filium ex Deo fuisse, non reipsa, sed figurative: quia in eo Deus futurum hominem geniturebat, mulierem exspectans, ex qua eum gigneret: Cum Ario, τὸν λόγον[?], tum cepisse existere, cum mundus creatus est, ac etiam ideam quandam fuisse ex tribus increatis Elementis compositam: Cum Eutyche, conceptum fuisse Filium in utero virginis ex ipsa verbi essentia, in carne transeunte, qua postea in deitatem fuerit absorpta: Cum Marcione etiam, non verum, sed imaginarium corpus Christo tribuebat, cum illud negaret ex femine Abrahae simpliciter fuisse genitum, sed partim etiam ex tribus illis Elementis conflatum, & substantiali quadam Dei facie, qua ab initio sanctis Patribus visa fuisset: Et cum Apollinari, animam Christi sane reipsa exinaniebat, cum illam diceret par-

page.notes: The printed "3" beside ")(" at the foot is read as the leaf number of the gathering signature, so no separate page number is given. The catchword "tim" is the start of "partim" on the next page. Doubtful readings: "Michaël" (the ligature may read Michaelis; marked [?]); the Greek "τὸν λόγον" after "Cum Ario," is small and was copied from the scan, marked [?]; "adeoq;" and "conflatū" are read from small type and the abbreviation marks may be faint. Long s is rendered as s throughout. Italic is set for the whole running text, as the scan shows; the marginal notes are set roman.
